name: Question 1
problem:
In a garden, $60%$ of the flowers are roses. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that if $100$ flowers are picked at random, then $70$ of them will be roses. Give your answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ | $\,0.9732\,$ | $\,0.9738\,$ |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ | $\,0.9788\,$ | $\,0.9793\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ | $\,0.9834\,$ | $\,0.9838\,$ |
worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=100$ and $p=0.6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =100\cdot 0.6 \\  & =60 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =100\cdot (1-0.6) \\  & =40 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(100)(0.6)=60
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(100)(0.6)(1-0.6)=24.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(60,24).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=70).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=70)≈P(69.5\le Y\le 70.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(69.5\le Y\le 70.5) & =P(\frac{69.5-60}{\sqrt{24}}\le Z\le \frac{70.5-60}{\sqrt{24}}) \\  & ≈P(1.94\le Z\le 2.14) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.14)-P(Z<1.94) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.14)-P(Z\le 1.94) \\  & =Φ(2.14)-Φ(1.94) \\  & =0.9838-0.9738 \\  & =0.010\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=70)≈0.010.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0102.$

EXPLANATION

Given a binomial random variable X∼B(n,p), if

  • np>5, and

  • n(1−p)>5,

we can approximate X as a normal random variable Y with mean μ=np and variance σ2=np(1−p), that is,

Y∼N(np,np(1−p)).

Here, we have n=100 and p=0.6. Therefore, np=100⋅0.6=60>5✓n(1−p)=100⋅(1−0.6)=40>5.✓ So, we can approximate our binomial random variable X with a normal random variable Y with mean

μ=np=(100)(0.6)=60

and variance

σ2=np(1−p)=(100)(0.6)(1−0.6)=24.

That is, we can approximate X by Y∼N(60,24).

Now, we can approximate the desired probability P(X=70). Using a continuity correction, we have

P(X=70)≈P(69.5≤Y≤70.5).

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by z-scoring:

P(69.5≤Y≤70.5)=P(69.5−6024≤Z≤70.5−6024)≈P(1.94≤Z≤2.14)=P(Z≤2.14)−P(Z<1.94)=P(Z≤2.14)−P(Z≤1.94)=Φ(2.14)−Φ(1.94)=0.9838−0.9738=0.010

Therefore,

P(X=70)≈0.010.

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of 0.0102.
